newsitem.title: FRANCE: POLL - French say Chirac should keep active role.
newsitem.headline: POLL - French say Chirac should keep active role.

text.p: With the left now in power, most French people say conservative President Jacques Chirac should still speak out on policy but they also back a referendum on a plan to cut two years from his term, a poll said on Wednesday.

A CSA survey for the weekly L'Evenement du Jeudi found that 63 percent wanted Chirac to hold a referendum on a proposal by the new leftist goverment to cut the presidential term to five years from seven, starting with him.

Chirac has already completed two years of his term, working with a like-minded government. Before his election in 1995, Chirac too had indicated that he believed the presidential term should be cut from seven to five years. But he has not mentioned the issue since being voted to office.
The right was swept from power in a June 1 election, succeeded by a leftist alliance led by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.

Despite strong support for the referendum on term length, 66 percent said Chirac should remain involved in developing policy on negotiations with Germany aimed at European economic and monetary union rather than leave the field to Jospin.
Fifty percent said he should have a say in the formulation of economic and social policy.
Separately, a Gallup poll found Chirac's approval rating higher than his disapproval score for the first time since May 1996.
The survey conducted for the weekly L'Express said 47 percent were pleased by his action as president while 39 percent were unhappy and 14 percent expressed no opinion.
It found that 59 percent approved of the performance of Jospin, who has been in power just five weeks, compared to 26 percent who said they were dissastisfied and 15 percent who expressed no opinion.
Jospin's score was about in line with other recent French prime ministers after a few weeks in office, Gallup said.
The CSA poll relied on surveys of 1,006 individuals aged 18 and over, who were questioned on Monday. Gallup interviewed 962 people 18 and above on last Friday and Saturday.
